limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.

judgment.argument: Nothing has been played. Table record, pilot feel and Forge are all withheld, so the measured components stand on a goldfish with no blockers and no removal. That blind spot cuts both ways for a blink deck, and I find nothing cited that argues a direction, so I sit at the measured line. The measured gaps are already priced: resilience reads 9 answer cards and construction carries the audit's counts, so I do not count them a second time. The audit's 0 on threat density is a tag-based count; the context names payoffs such as Avenger and Ballista that it may not see, so whether the deck has a finisher gap is an open question, not a finding. The one unmeasured fact is the context's own: the weak point is that the engine is the commander. It has no figure behind it, so it moves nothing here. The thesis (stack entry triggers, counters as a mana sink) is coherent on paper, but the context calls how well the counters plan works unmeasured, so it earns no credit either. This number says only that the instruments and the record agree and that play will have to decide it.
